title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: Picture 23's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$004B, channel 0's script at +$000E and 0 for channels 1, 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 20 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 10, frame 1 then 1, frame 2 then 5, frame 2 then 1, frame 1 then 20, frame 3 then 2, frame 3 then 8, frame 3 then 4, frame 4 then 15, frame 2 then 5, frame 5 then 3, frame 3 then 18, frame 1 then 20, frame 4 then 3, frame 5 then 1, frame 5 then 1, frame 3 then 12, frame 1 then 1, frame 2 then 7, frame 2 then 4. One pass takes 141 steps.

Picture 23's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $04 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 22 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 23, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2, 5, 13 and 18: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 2 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 23, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 3, 4, 10, 19 and 20: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 3 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 23, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 6, 7, 8, 12 and 17: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 6 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 23, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 9 and 14: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 6 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 23, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 11, 15 and 16: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 5 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 23's own packed bytes decode to, the 824th byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
